articles.title: 5 Signs Your Website Is Quietly Costing You Customers
articles.metaTitle: 5 Signs Your Website Is Costing You Customers | JindraWebDev
articles.metaDescription: Slow load times, no mobile layout, and buried contact info are silently turning visitors away. Here's how to spot the problem and what to fix first.
articles.excerpt: A slow, cluttered, or hard-to-navigate website doesn't just look bad — it actively pushes potential customers toward your competitors. Here are the five most common culprits and how to fix them.
articles.quickAnswer: The most common website problems that cost small businesses customers are slow load times, no mobile-friendly layout, unclear calls to action, buried contact information, and outdated content. Fixing even one or two of these can measurably improve how many visitors turn into inquiries.

faq.question: How fast should a small business website load?
faq.answer: Aim for under 3 seconds on mobile. Every extra second of load time measurably increases the chance a visitor leaves before your page even finishes loading.

faq.question: Do I really need a mobile-friendly website?
faq.answer: Yes — for most small, local businesses, more than half of visitors arrive on a phone. If your site isn't built mobile-first, you're likely losing the majority of your traffic before they see what you offer.

articles.title: What Recent Google Business Profile Changes Mean for Small-Town Businesses
articles.metaTitle: Google Business Profile Changes: What Small-Town Businesses Need to Know | JindraWebDev
articles.metaDescription: Google keeps tweaking how local businesses show up in search. Here's a plain-English breakdown of what changed and what to update on your profile this month.
articles.excerpt: Google Business Profile is often the first thing a potential customer sees about your business — before your website. Here's what's changed recently and what to check today.
articles.quickAnswer: Google periodically changes how it verifies, ranks, and displays local business profiles. Small-town businesses should regularly check their category accuracy, hours, photos, and review responses, since these directly affect whether they show up in local map searches.

faq.question: How often should I update my Google Business Profile?
faq.answer: Check it at least monthly — hours, photos, and posts. Google favors profiles that show ongoing activity over ones that were set up once and forgotten.
